turns.t: Sorry I'm late. Parking. ~
No problem at all. Come in. What can I do for you today? ~
Eye drops. I want to check them.
Which eye drops? ~
The ones I'm using. For dryness.
What are they called?
Artificial tears. Four times a day. Maybe two drops each time? I'm not sure.
How long have you used them? ~
A few months. ~
And what made you want to check them? ~
I think I'm allergic to something in them.
Why do you say that?
Red eyes. Itchy. After I put them in.
Do you know what the reaction is to?
The preservative, I think. The label says so.
That would make sense. Do you have any allergies that I should know about?
Just that. And penicillin.
Penicillin, I'll note that, too. Can you tell me about it?
Rash. As a kid.
Right. I'll put both on your file. ~
Okay. ~
Anything in your health history I should know about?
Dry eye. That's it.
Have you had any eye surgery?
LASIK. In 2016.
Do you work on a computer?
Graphic designer. All day.
How many hours? ~
Ten. ~
Right. Let me explain. Many eye drops contain a preservative, to keep the bottle fresh. In some people it irritates the eye with regular use. ~
That's what I thought. ~
I think your eyes are being irritated by the preservative, probably on top of the dry eye from screens and from the LASIK.
Okay. ~
There are preservative-free versions, in single-use vials. You could ask the pharmacy for those.
Are they expensive? ~
A bit more, but they're much gentler. ~
Fine. ~
And take a break from the screen every twenty minutes, look out the window for twenty seconds.
I forget. ~
Set a timer on your computer. ~
Good idea. ~
I'd like to see you again in six weeks to see how your eyes are.
Okay. Six weeks. ~
Anything else? ~
No. Thanks. ~
